fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of parked vehicles so fire and emergency apparatus can reach the residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Maintain enough width and overhead clearance along the access drive for a fire truck to pass without stopping to reposition.
• Keep a turnaround area clear near the residence so apparatus can exit without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Post the property address visibly at the road and again near the residence in case responders enter the property but lose sight of the street marker.
• Keep the area around the detached structure accessible so responders can reach it without crossing through the landscaped area or open terrain without a clear path.
• If the perimeter fencing has a gate across the access drive, keep that gate unlocked or install a knox-box so responders are not delayed at the entrance.
• Identify and mark any secondary foot path or vehicle route around the rear of the property to give responders an alternative if the main driveway becomes blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between the canopy and the building.
• Cut back ground vegetation around the base of the structure to reduce the amount of low-growing material close to the walls.
• Remove or mow dry ground vegetation along both sides of the driveway to reduce the concentration of burnable material along the travel route.
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that overhang or lean over the driveway surface to keep the full width and height of the route clear for vehicle access.
• Keep the driveway surface and edges clear of fallen branches, dead leaves, and other debris that could ignite along the access route.
• Thin shrubs and trees at the driveway entrance to maintain clear sightlines and an unobstructed entry point for vehicles.
• Separate any shrub groupings near the structure so that plants are not growing in continuous masses that connect directly to the building.
• Keep the open green space near the structure mowed short to maintain separation between taller surrounding vegetation and the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so that it remains easy to identify quickly from the road, given the single access route to the property.
